/-!
# Combining the point measurements

This module constructs the projective joint X/Z point measurements and defines
their scalar linear coarse-graining. The latter is
the genuine postprocessing of a complete measurement on each heterogeneous
player space.

## References

The construction is `lem:qld-4-10` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, with paper source
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
The coarse-graining is `lem:qld-4-12` in the same blueprint, with paper source
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:993-1011`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- A pair of source points and the two scalar coefficients used by the
extended point measurement. -/
abbrev ExtendedPointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
    (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P)

namespace CombinedPointsWitness

/-- Coarse-grain a joint point measurement by `(a,b) |-> alpha*a + beta*b`
on the selected player side.  This is the concrete measurement of
`lem:qld-4-12`, paper lines 993--1011. -/
noncomputable def extendedQ {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ)
    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)
    (alpha beta : PauliScalar P) :
    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  (points.Q side x z).postprocess fun ab => alpha * ab.1 + beta * ab.2

end CombinedPointsWitness

/-- Construction of the projective joint point measurements of
`lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709.  The witness retains both ordered
products and all four directed heterogeneous placement comparisons.

The construction works on the original expanded local spaces: the sandwich
POVM `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b`, formed directly with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, is
close to the ordered product by the field-valued commutation estimate
(`expPoint_comm`), self-consistent between opposite placements
(`sandwich_offDiagonal_le_sandwichDefectBound`), and is made projective for
each point pair by the orthonormalization lemma
(`exists_projective_close_sandwich`); the three consistency conclusions follow
by the triangle inequality (`chain_bounds`).  The source's route through the
binary refinements and the quantum linearity theorem is not used, because
that route needs zero-state padding of the strategy, which is not part of the
setting; see `rem:linearity-import` and
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.  The error is
`K ε^{1/8}` for a universal constant `K`. -/
theorem exists_combinedPointsWitness :
    ∃ deltaQ : ℝ -> ℝ, IsPolyErr deltaQ ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
        Nonempty (CombinedPointsWitness S (deltaQ ε)) := by
  obtain ⟨C₀, hC₀, h₀⟩ := ProjectiveSetting.avg_sandwichDefectBound_le
  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁, h₁⟩ := ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le
  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂, h₂⟩ := ProjectiveSetting.expPoint_comm
  obtain ⟨C₃, hC₃, h₃⟩ := ProjectiveSetting.ordered_cross_dist_le
  -- the universal constant of the final error `K ε^{1/8}`
  set K : ℝ := 12 * (440 * (2 * C₀)) + 20 * C₁ + 16 * C₃ + 4 * C₂ with hK
  have hK4 : (4 : ℝ) ≤ K := by rw [hK]; nlinarith
  refine ⟨fun ε => K * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ),
    ⟨K, 1 / 8, by linarith, by norm_num, fun x hx =>
      ⟨mul_nonneg (by linarith) (Real.rpow_nonneg hx _), le_rfl⟩⟩, ?_⟩
  intro P ε S
  have hε : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε := by
    have hv := WinImplications.strategy_value_le_one S.toStrategy
    have hw := S.win
    linarith
  obtain ⟨Qa, hQa, hQaR⟩ := S.exists_projective_close_sandwich_alice
  obtain ⟨Qb, hQb, hQbR⟩ := S.exists_projective_close_sandwich_bob
  -- the joint measurements on the two sides
  let Q : (side : PlayerSide) → PointPair P →
      Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
    fun side => match side with
      | .alice => Qa
      | .bob => Qb
  have hQproj : ∀ side xz, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (Q side xz) := by
    intro side xz
    cases side
    · exact hQa xz
    · exact hQb xz
  -- the closeness of `Q` to the sandwich on every placement
  set η : ℝ := 440 * Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) with hη
  have hbound : ∀ p₁ p₂ : Placement, p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
      220 * Real.rpow (avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
        (S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ η := by
    intro p₁ p₂ hopp
    have hnn : 0 ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
        (S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂) :=
      avgOver_nonneg _ _ (S.sandwichDefectBound_nonneg p₁ p₂)
    have hr : Real.rpow (avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
        (S.sandwichDefectBound p₁ p₂)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
        Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) :=
      Real.rpow_le_rpow hnn (h₀ P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp) (by norm_num)
    have hr0 : 0 ≤ Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) :=
      Real.rpow_nonneg (by positivity) _
    rw [hη]
    nlinarith
  have hQR : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
        S.place p ((Q p.side xz).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      S.psiHat ≤ η := by
    intro p
    cases p
    · exact le_trans hQaR (hbound .AA' .BA'' trivial)
    · exact le_trans hQbR (hbound .BA'' .AA' trivial)
    · rw [ProjectiveSetting.opFamilyDistSq_place_BB'_eq_BA'']
      exact le_trans hQbR (hbound .BA'' .AA' trivial)
    · rw [ProjectiveSetting.opFamilyDistSq_place_AB''_eq_AA']
      exact le_trans hQaR (hbound .AA' .BA'' trivial)
  have hchain := fun (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂) =>
    S.chain_bounds Q η C₁ C₂ C₃ hQR (h₁ P ε S) (h₂ P ε S) (h₃ P ε S) p₁ p₂ hopp
  -- the numeric bound on the longest chain, in the two regimes of `ε`
  have hηnn : 0 ≤ η := by
    rw [hη]
    exact mul_nonneg (by norm_num)
      (Real.rpow_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (add_nonneg hε (Real.sqrt_nonneg ε))) _)
  have hs : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
  have htotal : 12 * η + 20 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 16 * (C₃ * ε) +
      4 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) ≤ K * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) ∨ 1 < ε := by
    by_cases hε1 : ε ≤ 1
    · left
      obtain ⟨hε8, hs8, hq8⟩ := error_terms_le_rpow_eighth hε hε1 hC₀
      rw [hη, hK]
      nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hq8 (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 440),
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hs8 (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) ≤ C₁),
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hs8 (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) ≤ C₂),
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hε8 (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) ≤ C₃)]
    · right
      exact lt_of_not_ge hε1
  have hK8 : 1 < ε → (4 : ℝ) ≤ K * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
    intro hε1
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) :=
      Real.one_le_rpow (le_of_lt hε1) (by norm_num)
    nlinarith
  have hsub1 : 2 * η + 4 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 4 * (C₃ * ε) ≤
      12 * η + 20 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 16 * (C₃ * ε) + 4 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
    nlinarith
  have hsub2 : 4 * η + 8 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 8 * (C₃ * ε) +
      2 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) ≤
      12 * η + 20 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 16 * (C₃ * ε) + 4 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
    nlinarith
  -- square-summability of the families, for the trivial bound
  have hsqQ : ∀ (p : Placement) (xz : PointPair P),
      (∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
        (S.place p ((Q p.side xz).effect ab))ᴴ *
          S.place p ((Q p.side xz).effect ab)) ≤ 1 :=
    fun p xz => S.sum_place_effect_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one p _ (hQproj p.side xz)
  have hsqXZ : ∀ (p : Placement) (xz : PointPair P),
      (∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
        (S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))ᴴ *
        S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)) ≤ 1 := by
    intro p xz
    refine le_of_eq ?_
    simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]

/-!
# The ordered point product on a single placement

The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
triangle inequality twice.

## References

The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
between the two members of each pair. -/
theorem Placement.exists_isOpposite (p : Placement) :
    ∃ q : Placement, p.IsOpposite q ∧ q.IsOpposite p := by
  cases p with
  | AA' => exact ⟨.BA'', trivial, trivial⟩
  | BA'' => exact ⟨.AA', trivial, trivial⟩
  | BB' => exact ⟨.AB'', trivial, trivial⟩
  | AB'' => exact ⟨.BB', trivial, trivial⟩

/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
theorem CombinedPointsWitness.orderedZX_dist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    {ε δ : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
    (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) (p : Placement) :
    opFamilyDistSq
        (uniformDistribution
          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
        (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
        (fun xz ab => S.place p
          ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
            (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * δ := by
  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hqp⟩ := p.exists_isOpposite
  have htri := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le
    (uniformDistribution
      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    (fun xz ab => S.place q ((points.Q q.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    (fun xz ab => S.place p
      ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    S.psiHat δ δ (points.self_consistent p q hpq)
    (points.consistent_ZX q p hqp)
  linarith

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Coordinate blocks of a truncated extended direction

This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended
vector by zeroing the coordinates that precede the stored coordinate index,
so each source block is again a prefix truncation: when the stored index is
the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,
preceding blocks vanish, and later blocks remain untruncated.
The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
two identified scalar fields.

## References

The block computations support `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
The truncation is the prefix restriction of blueprint
`def:ld-question-distribution`; the coordinate blocks are those of
blueprint `def:combine-map`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding the first coordinate changes nothing.
Blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
theorem prefixProjection_of_val_zero {L : LdParams} {i : Fin L.m}
    (hi : i.val = 0) (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
    prefixProjection i v = v := by
  funext j
  simp [prefixProjection, hi]

/-! ## The `X` block of a truncated extended direction -/

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at an `X`-block
coordinate is the `X` block truncated at that coordinate of the source space.
Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projX (directPointToPauli P

      prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i (projX (directPointToPauli P v)) := by

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at a `Z`-block
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)

/-!
# Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction

This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
procedure of the sub-line lemma. First, for independent uniform inputs `u` in
the ambient coordinate space and `t` in the scalar field, the point
`lineRepMap v u + t • v` is uniform. This map on ambient-point--parameter pairs
has fibers of size `q`: for nonzero `v`, `u` varies over a coset of the span of
`v`, while its canonical representative and `t` are fixed; for zero `v`, `u`
is fixed and `t` is free. Second, the two coordinate
blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
coordinates.

## References

The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
The canonical representative map is blueprint
`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
blueprint `def:combine-map`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/

/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
-/
theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
  exact h.symm

/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/

/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
`q` elements in the ambient-point--parameter domain: for a nonzero direction
the parameter and canonical representative are fixed, while the input point
varies over a coset of the span of the direction. For the zero direction the
input point is fixed and the parameter is free. Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul {K : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) :
    (uniformDistribution ((Fin m → K) × K)).map
        (fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) =
      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card K) fun x => ?_
  by_cases hv : v = 0
  · subst hv
    have hfilter :
        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
            fun w => lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) w.1 + w.2 • (0 : Fin m → K)
              = x)
          = ({x} : Finset (Fin m → K)) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset K) := by
      ext w
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
        Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton, and_true, smul_zero,
        add_zero, lineRepMap_zero_apply]
    rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
    simp
  · have hinj : Function.Injective
        (fun c : K => (lineRepMap v x + c • v, directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
      intro c₁ c₂ hc
      have hc' : c₁ • v = c₂ • v := by
        have h := congrArg Prod.fst hc
        simpa using h
      have hsub : (c₁ - c₂) • v = 0 := by
        rw [sub_smul, hc', sub_self]
      rcases smul_eq_zero.mp hsub with h | h
      · exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
      · exact absurd h hv
    have himg :
        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
            fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v = x)
          = (Finset.univ : Finset K).image
              (fun c => (lineRepMap v x + c • v,
                directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
      ext w
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image]
      constructor
      · intro hw
        have hrep : lineRepMap v w.1 = lineRepMap v x := by

/-!
# Z-point deficits of the evaluated pair-line measurement

The proof of `lem:claim-17-3` bounds, after its Cauchy--Schwarz step, the
deficit of the overlap between the evaluated pair-line measurement and the
expanded `Z`-point measurement at the `Z`-point of the sample.
This module derives that deficit from the
consistency of the evaluated pair-line measurement with the completed joint
point measurement and from the closeness of the joint point measurement to the
ordered point products. The derivation inserts the joint point measurement
on the point side, replaces it by the ordered product whose trailing factor is
the retained point effect, and sums the other factor, at the cost of three
square roots. The deficit is first bounded over an arbitrary probability
law on pairs of line-point pairs and then over a product of two restricted
line-point laws, whose point marginal is the uniform pair.
The `_at` variants retain arbitrary opposite placements, including Bob at
`BBprime` and Alice at `ABdoubleprime`. The original statements are unchanged
specializations; register commutation does not assume symmetry of the state.
The separate concrete X-marginal argument used for Claim 17-2 is in
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`.

## References

The Z deficit is the quantity bounded in the proof of `lem:claim-17-3`
in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the
consistency input is `lem:qld-xz-lines` and the ordered products are those of
`lem:qld-4-10`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

noncomputable section

/-! ## Completed point pairs -/

/-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
theorem sum_option_prod_eq_of_none {β γ : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    (F : Option β × Option γ → ℝ) (h1 : ∀ o2, F (none, o2) = 0)
    (h2 : ∀ o1, F (o1, none) = 0) :
    (∑ o, F o) = ∑ bc : β × γ, F (some bc.1, some bc.2) := by
  calc (∑ o : Option β × Option γ, F o)
      = ∑ o1 : Option β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (o1, o2) := Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := F)
    _ = (∑ o2 : Option γ, F (none, o2)) +
          ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := Fintype.sum_option _
    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ o2 : Option γ, F (some b, o2) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero fun o2 _ => h1 o2, zero_add]
    _ = ∑ b : β, (F (some b, none) + ∑ c : γ, F (some b, some c)) :=
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => Fintype.sum_option _

        (Fintype.sum_prod_type (f := fun bc : β × γ => F (some bc.1, some bc.2))).symm

/-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
evaluations. -/
theorem completedPair_effect_some {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (bc : β × γ) :
    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect (some bc.1, some bc.2) =
      Q.effect bc := by
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
    show (Finset.univ.filter fun cd : β × γ =>
        (some cd.1, some cd.2) = (some bc.1, some bc.2)) = {bc} by
      ext cd; simp [Prod.ext_iff, eq_comm]]
  simp

/-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
the completion. -/
theorem completedPair_effect_eq_zero {β γ d : Type*} [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (Q : Measurement (β × γ) d) (o : Option β × Option γ)
    (ho : ∀ bc : β × γ, (some bc.1, some bc.2) ≠ o) :
    (Q.postprocess fun ab => (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect o = 0 := by
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun bc hbc =>
    absurd (Finset.mem_filter.mp hbc).2 (ho bc)

/-!
# Approximate commutation of the field-valued expanded point measurements

The approximate commutation of `lem:qld-comm-cons` is stated for the binary
refinements `M^{(Point,W),u,r}_b` of the expanded point measurements.  The
combined point measurements of `lem:qld-4-10` are built here directly from the
`F_q`-valued measurements `M^{(Point,W),u}_a`, so the commutation estimate is
transferred to them.  The transfer is exact: since
`M^{(Point,X),x}_a = E_r (-1)^{tr(ar)} X^r(x)` and
`M^{(Point,Z),z}_b = E_s (-1)^{tr(bs)} Z^s(z)`, the commutator of the two
measurement effects is the Fourier transform, in the outcome pair `(a, b)`,
of the commutators of the expanded observables, and Parseval's identity for
the additive characters of `F_q` turns the sum over `(a, b)` of the squared
norms into the average over `(r, s)` of the squared norms of the observable
commutators.  No factor depending on `q` is lost.

## Main results

* `sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal`: Parseval's identity for an orthogonal
  system of coefficients.
* `sum_fixedCharacter_mul`: Fourier cancellation for the fixed trace character.
* `expPoint_comm`: the field-valued expanded point measurements approximately
  commute on every register placement, with the error of
  `lem:qld-comm-cons`.

`lem:qld-comm-cons`, blueprint

`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:466-505`; the

lines 384--418.  The role of the transfer in the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` is

/-! ## Parseval's identity for an orthogonal system of coefficients -/

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:qld-4-10`: if the coefficient
columns `j ↦ c j i`, indexed by `i`, are orthogonal with common
squared norm `N`, then the squared norms of the weighted sums
`∑ i, c j i • v i` add up to `N` times the squared norms of the `v i`. -/
theorem sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal {I J E : Type*} [Fintype I]
    [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    (c : J → I → ℂ) (N : ℝ)
    (horth : ∀ i i', ∑ j, (starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i' =
      if i = i' then (N : ℂ) else 0)
    (v : I → E) :
    ∑ j, ‖∑ i, c j i • v i‖ ^ 2 = N * ∑ i, ‖v i‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hnorm : ∀ x : E, ‖x‖ ^ 2 = (inner ℂ x x).re := fun x => by
    simpa using (inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) x).symm
  have hj : ∀ j, ‖∑ i, c j i • v i‖ ^ 2 =
      (∑ i, ∑ i', ((starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i') *
        inner ℂ (v i) (v i')).re := by
    intro j
    rw [hnorm, sum_inner]
    simp only [inner_sum, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right]
    congr 1
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i' _ => ?_
    ring
  have hsum : ∑ j, ∑ i, ∑ i', ((starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i') *
      inner ℂ (v i) (v i') = ∑ i, (N : ℂ) * inner ℂ (v i) (v i) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    calc ∑ i', ∑ j, ((starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i') * inner ℂ (v i) (v i')
        = ∑ i', (∑ j, (starRingEnd ℂ) (c j i) * c j i') *

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedAverage.lean:1665:+transfers to one restricted component.  The line-point law places weight
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedAverage.lean:1666:+`1 / 2` on each of its two kinds and, inside each kind, weight `1 / m` on each

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedMixture.lean:1901:+This module proves that the axis-parallel and diagonal line-point laws are the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedMixture.lean:1902:+uniform mixtures of their coordinate-index restrictions.  The identity rests on

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedMixture.lean:1905:+line conditioning map keeps that seed.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2172:+# Rewriting rules for dependent mixtures of finite distributions
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2173:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2174:+This module records the elementary rewriting rules for the dependent mixture
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2175:+of finite distributions that the sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2176:+uses: a mixture indexed along a push-forward is the mixture indexed along the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2177:+original law, iterated mixtures associate, a mixture is unchanged when the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2178:+mixed family is changed only outside the index support, a mixture of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2179:+constant family is that constant, a product with a fixed independent factor
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2180:+distributes over a mixture, and an equal two-term mixture is the mixture
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2181:+indexed by a uniform pair of labels.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2182:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2183:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2184:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:2185:+The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2390:+This module isolates the independent generating blocks of the restricted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2391:+line-point laws used by the sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma.  A

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2416:+/-! ## Uniform laws on products -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2462:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: normalized restriction depends on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2463:+restricted law only through its support and weights.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2464:+`lem:qld-sublines`, paper

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2526:+/-- Conditioning a uniform product law on an event of its second factor leaves

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2553:+/-! ## The block decomposition of an ambient low-degree vector -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2555:+/-- Split an ambient low-degree vector into its point block and its

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBlocks.lean:2701:+/-- The axis-line decoder read on the block decomposition. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2772:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2773:+# The branch data of the sub-line sampling procedure
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2774:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2775:+The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma draws a line kind, a stored
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2776:+extended coordinate, and an unrestricted extended direction, and forms from
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2777:+them the direction of the extended line: the elementary direction at the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2778:+stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2779:+coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the diagonal
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2780:+branch.  The two source lines are then read off the two coordinate blocks.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2781:+This module fixes the coordinate index that each source line must carry: the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2782:+stored coordinate itself when it belongs to that block, the first coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2783:+otherwise.  With that choice the source block of the extended direction always
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2784:+lies in the line spanned by the corresponding source direction, which is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2785:+incidence hypothesis of the two projection lemmas.  The module also records
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2786:+that moving an extended point to its canonical representative does not change
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2787:+the canonical representative of either of its source blocks.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBranch.lean:2788:+

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3195:+# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3196:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3197:+This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3198:+kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3199:+and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3200:+independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3201:+two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3202:+diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3203:+decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3204:+from the two seeds.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3205:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3206:+The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineConstruct.lean:3207:+of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3755:+# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3756:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3757:+This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3758:+the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3759:+is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3760:+coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3761:+the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3762:+point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3763:+commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3764:+canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3765:+field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineExtended.lean:3766:+the same three coordinate ranges.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4371:+# Products and push-forwards of finite distributions
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4372:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4373:+The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma presents one law both as an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4374:+independent product of its generating blocks and as a dependent mixture over
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4375:+one of those blocks.  This module records the three rewriting rules that pass
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4376:+between the two presentations: a push-forward of the first factor of a product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4377:+is a push-forward of the product, a product with a probability law in the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4378:+second factor has the first factor as its marginal, and a push-forward of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineProduct.lean:4379:+product is the dependent mixture of the push-forwards of its second factor.

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5762:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5763:+# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5764:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5765:+The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5766:+the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5767:+scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5768:+coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5769:+of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5770:+This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5771:+source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5772:+reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5773:+line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5774:+same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5775:+

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5781:+The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5793:+/-! ## The identification of the two scalar fields as a bijection -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5795:+/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5796:+source scalar field on one source block, presented as a bijection.  Blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5797:+`def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5798:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5810:+/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5811:+source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5812:+Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5813:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5826:+/-- The `X` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `X`

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5835:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5840:+/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5842:+/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5882:+/-! ## Resampling a uniform point along a line -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5887:+random point.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineTransport.lean:5888:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5913:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5914:+# Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5915:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5916:+This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5917:+procedure of the sub-line lemma. First, for independent uniform inputs `u` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5918:+the ambient coordinate space and `t` in the scalar field, the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5919:+`lineRepMap v u + t • v` is uniform. This map on ambient-point--parameter pairs
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5920:+has fibers of size `q`: for nonzero `v`, `u` varies over a coset of the span of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5921:+`v`, while its canonical representative and `t` are fixed; for zero `v`, `u`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5922:+is fixed and `t` is free. Second, the two coordinate
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5923:+blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5924:+corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5925:+carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5926:+coordinates.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5927:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5928:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5929:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5930:+The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5931:+blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5932:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5933:+The canonical representative map is blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5934:+`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5935:+blueprint `def:combine-map`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5936:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5946:+/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5948:+/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5949:+`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5950:+is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5951:+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5952:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5960:+/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5962:+/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5963:+canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5964:+the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5965:+`q` elements in the ambient-point--parameter domain: for a nonzero direction
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5966:+the parameter and canonical representative are fixed, while the input point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5967:+varies over a coset of the span of the direction. For the zero direction the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:5969:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineUniform.lean:6032:+/-! ## Injectivity of the two block embeddings -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6284:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6285:+# The ordered point product on a single placement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6286:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6287:+The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6288:+with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6289:+The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6290:+families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6291:+joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6292:+triangle inequality twice.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6293:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6294:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6295:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6296:+The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6297:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6298:+`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6299:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6300:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6311:+/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6312:+between the two members of each pair. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6321:+/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OrderedPoints.lean:6322:+`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6359:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6360:+# Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6361:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6362:+The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6363:+overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6364:+are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6365:+the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6366:+arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6367:+is not itself a measurement.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6368:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6369:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6370:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6371:+The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6372:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6373:+step at paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6374:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6375:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6384:+/-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6385:+complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6386:+state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6499:+/-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6501:+/-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6502:+Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6503:+`⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6504:+proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6505:+the square root of the line effect, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6506:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6541:+/-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6542:+positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6543:+two diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6572:+/-- The averaged form of the preceding estimate: the average over a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6573:+distribution of the outcome sums of `Re ⟨u, A v⟩` is bounded by the product of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6574:+the square roots of the two averaged diagonal sums. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6624:+/-! ## Quadratic forms against projections -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6626:+/-- The real quadratic form is invariant under the conjugate transpose. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6636:+/-- Conjugating an operator transfers the outer operator to the state vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6647:+/-- For a projection `B` commuting with `A`, the quadratic form of `A` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6648:+`B ψ` is the quadratic form of `A B` in `ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6656:+/-- The quadratic form of an operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6657:+the squared norm of the vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6664:+/-- The effects of a complete measurement have total quadratic form one on a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6665:+unit vector. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6677:+/-- Weighting a complete measurement by commuting projections cannot exceed
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6678:+the total mass one. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6706:+/-! ## Replacing a factor under the weight of a measurement -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6708:+/-- Cauchy--Schwarz with the measurement as weight: for projections `B`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6709:+commuting with the effects of `A`, the averaged overlap of `A` against the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6710:+product `B C` is bounded by the square roots of the averaged overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6711:+against `B` and of the averaged quadratic form of `A` in `C ψ`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6712:+Cauchy--Schwarz step of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6713:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6756:+/-- Deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate: for projections `B` and `C`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6757:+commuting with the effects of `A`, replacing the factor `C B` by `C` inside an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6758:+overlap weighted by the complete measurement `A` changes the average by at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6759:+most the square root of the deficit `1 - E Σ_a ⟨A_a B_a⟩`.  This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6760:+estimate used in the proof of `lem:claim-17-2` and, with `C = Id`, in the proof
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6761:+of `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6762:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6811:+/-- The deficit form of the Cauchy--Schwarz estimate with the product family
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6812:+`C B` supplied as one family `CB`, which is convenient when the product is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6813:+formed on a local space before being placed. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6828:+/-- Inserting an arbitrary operator family `W` after a projection family `R`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6829:+commuting with the effects of `A` costs at most the square root of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6830:+averaged squared norms of `W ψ`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6858:+/-- The mirror image of the preceding estimate: an operator family `W`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6859:+commuting with the effects of `A`, inserted before a commuting projection
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6860:+family `R`, costs at most the square root of the averaged squared norms of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/OverlapGap.lean:6861:+`Wᴴ ψ`. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6935:+# Sub-line averages of the Z-point overlap
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6936:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6937:+The overlap of the paired-line measurement with the expanded `Z`-point effect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6938:+depends only on the two source lines and the `Z`-point. The separate Z marginal
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6939:+of the auxiliary subline law is a mixture of products of restricted line-point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6940:+laws, with the fresh X point unused. Regrouping the line answers by evaluation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6941:+at that point permits the Z deficit estimates of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6942:+`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.ZEvalDeficit` to apply component by component.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6943:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6944:+The `_at` estimates and `zPointOverlapAt` retain arbitrary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6945:+opposite placements. The original overlap definitions and first-player
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6946:+statements are unchanged. Only the separate Z marginal mixture is used.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6947:+The concrete X-marginal argument for Claim 17-2 is in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6948:+`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ConcreteXDeficit`. Transport of the auxiliary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6949:+subline law to the paper's carrier remains open; see
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6950:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_subline-claims-line-marginal.tex`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6951:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6952:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6953:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6954:+The statements support the auxiliary `lem:claim-17-3-direct-real`, near
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6955:+the source `lem:claim-17-3` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6956:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6957:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`; the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6969:+/-! ## Regrouping the line answers by their evaluations -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6971:+/-- Summing a paired-line answer against a family of point effects that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6972:+depends on the answer only through its two evaluations is summing the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6973:+evaluation classes of the paired-line measurement against that family.  This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6974:+is the fiber regrouping of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-1`, `lem:claim-17-2`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6975:+and `lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:6976:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2830`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7063:+/-- The sub-line average of a function of the two source lines and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7064:+`X`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7065:+of two restricted line-point laws, the `X`-point being the point of the first

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7067:+`lem:claim-17-2`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7068:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1201`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7097:+/-- The sub-line average of a function of the two source lines and the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7098:+`Z`-point of the sampled extended point is a mixture of averages over products
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7099:+of two restricted line-point laws, the `Z`-point being the point of the second
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7100:+factor.  This is the use of Property~2 of `lem:qld-sublines` in the proof of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7101:+`lem:claim-17-3`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7102:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1204-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7131:+/-! ## The two one-point overlaps -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7138:+/-- The overlap of the paired-line measurement at two source lines with the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7139:+expanded `Z`-point effect at a point, summed over the line answers.  This is

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7150:+/-- The original first-player specialization of the placed overlap. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/SubLineZDeficit.lean:7158:+/-- At a pair of line-point pairs, the `Z`-point overlap is the overlap of the

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7663:+/-! ## Completed point pairs -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7665:+/-- A sum over completed outcome pairs of a function vanishing on both `none`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7666:+classes is the sum over the uncompleted pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7685:+/-- The completed joint measurement has the joint effect on a pair of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7686:+evaluations. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7698:+/-- The completed joint measurement vanishes on outcomes outside the image of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7699:+the completion. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7709:+/-- The completion of a projective joint measurement is projective. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7727:+/-- A placed projection is a projection. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7737:+/-- Every effect of the completed expanded point measurement is a projection,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7738:+the `none` effect being zero. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7751:+/-- The completed joint point measurement and a completed point product differ
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7752:+only on outcome pairs with two evaluations, so their placed state-dependent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7753:+squared distance is the one of the joint point measurement and the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7754:+product.  Blueprint `ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2651-2698`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7782:+/-- The completed `Z`-then-`X` point product vanishes on both `none` classes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7783:+and restricts to the ordered product on evaluated pairs. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7813:+/-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7815:+/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7816:+family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7817:+outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7818:+`W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7819:+within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7820:+with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7821:+`Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7822:+Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7823:+the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7824:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7944:+/-! ## The two placed deficits -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7947:+consistency display of `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ZEvalDeficit.lean:7957:+/-- The `Z`-point deficit of the evaluated pair-line measurement over a

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8694:+/-! ## Generic bipartite estimates -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8698:+/-- A projective effect is absorbed by the postprocessed effect of the fiber
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8699:+containing its own outcome. Formalization-only auxiliary for the projective

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8732:+/-- A left-placed projective family, compared with itself followed by a

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8773:+left-placed effect selected through a coarse-graining, is at most as far from
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8774:+it as the coarse-grained families are from each other. This is the projective
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8775:+refinement of `fact:add-a-proj2` on the reversed directed pair. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8820:+/-! ## Transport between the six registers and the bipartitions -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8823:+/-- On the `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition, an `AA'` placement followed by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/BipartiteTransport.lean:8882:+/-- On the `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition, an `AB''` placement followed by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9598:+# Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9599:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9600:+This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9601:+`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9602:+a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9603:+of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9604:+unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9605:+the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9606:+expanded-line consistency lemma.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9607:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9608:+Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9609:+these facts about evaluation without stating them.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9610:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9611:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9612:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9613:+The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9614:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9615:+manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9616:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9617:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9625:+/-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9626:+is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9634:+/-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9635:+evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9642:+/-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9643:+their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9644:+whenever both convolution factors do. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9651:+/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, the first summand evaluates to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9652:+the difference of their values. This is the converse direction used to identify
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9653:+the convolution fibers of an evaluation class. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9663:+/-- The partial evaluation returns `some a` exactly when the polynomial
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9664:+evaluates to `a`. This is the characterization that makes `evalOpt` the total
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9665:+form of the evaluation classes of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9680:+/-- The partial evaluation returns `none` exactly when no value is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9681:+determined. This is the outcome that completes the evaluation classes to a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9682:+measurement, written `[eval_u(·) = ⊥]` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9689:+/-- The partial evaluation of a sum of two evaluating line polynomials is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9690:+the sum of their values. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9699:+/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, so does the first summand,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9700:+with the difference of the two values. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9709:+/-- A point at which some line polynomial evaluates lies on the line. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9715:+/-- Off the line, no line polynomial evaluates, so every outcome falls in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Evaluation.lean:9716:+the `none` class. -/

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10531:+# Overlap of expanded line and expanded point measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10532:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10533:+This module computes the diagonal overlap, on the expanded state, between an
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10534:+expanded line measurement on one placement and the expanded point effects
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10535:+selected by evaluation at the sampled point on the opposite placement. Each
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10536:+product of convolution terms factorizes into a strategy overlap and an EPR
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10537:+overlap; the EPR overlap of a Pauli line projector with a Pauli point projector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10538:+vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and then
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10539:+equals the EPR overlap of the line projector alone. Summing over the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10540:+convolution fibers identifies the expanded overlap with the overlap of the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10541:+strategy's evaluation classes and its completed point measurement. This is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10542:+computation displayed in items 2 and 3 of the expanded-line consistency lemma.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10543:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10544:+The sections on the linearity of the state quadratic form, on register
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10545:+placements, and on the completed point measurements collect formalization-only
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10546:+auxiliaries: the source uses these facts without stating them.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:10547:+
