MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11470:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11471:+# Pauli-register line projectors
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11472:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11473:+This module constructs the projective measurement `tau^{W,line}` of one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11474:+generalized-Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction to a canonical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11475:+line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. It records that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11476:+the outcome projectors are orthogonal projections summing to the identity,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11477:+that they are symmetric matrices (so that they act identically on either half
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11478:+of an EPR pair), and that on an axis-parallel line they vanish outside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11479:+embedded degree-`d` subspace.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11480:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11481:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11482:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11483:+The projectors are `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` of `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11484:+with paper source
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11485:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. Their
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11486:+perfect self-consistency on an EPR pair is the ancillary input to item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11487:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11488:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11489:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11500:+/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11501:+restricts to `f` on `line`. This is `tau^{W,line}_f` in the proof of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11502:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11503:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11504:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11512:+/-- Pauli line projectors are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11513:+the ancillary measurement in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11514:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11522:+/-- The line coarse-graining of the generalized Pauli projectors is a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11523:+symmetric matrix. Symmetry is what makes the projector act identically on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11524:+either half of an EPR pair, and hence is the hypothesis behind the perfect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11525:+ancilla consistency used in `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11526:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11533:+/-- Pauli line projectors belonging to distinct line polynomials are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11534:+orthogonal, while each projector is idempotent. This is the ancillary product
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11535:+calculation in `def:expanded-line-measurement` and item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11536:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11537:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-558`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11566:+/-- The line fibers partition the complete family of Pauli eigenspace
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11567:+projectors. This is the completeness of the ancillary measurement in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11568:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11569:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11583:+/-- The projective line measurement on one Pauli register obtained by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11584:+measuring the generalized Pauli basis and restricting the low-degree encoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11585:+of the outcome to `line`. This is the ancillary measurement of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11586:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11587:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11594:+/-- The effects of the Pauli line measurement are the line projectors. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11599:+/-- On an axis-parallel line, Pauli line projectors vanish outside the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11600:+embedded degree-`d` subspace, because every restricted low-degree encoding has
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11601:+degree at most `d` there. This is the ancillary half of the last assertion of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11602:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11603:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11618:+/-! ## Interaction with the point projectors -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11620:+/-- On a point of the line, Pauli line projectors of non-evaluating
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11621:+polynomials vanish: every restricted low-degree encoding evaluates there.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11622:+Formalization-only auxiliary for items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11623:+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11640:+/-- A Pauli line projector followed by a Pauli point projector at a point of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11641:+the line is the line projector when the line polynomial evaluates to the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11642:+point value, and zero otherwise. This is the exact consistency
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11643:+`tau^{W,line}_{f''}` versus `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` in items 2 and 3 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11644:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11645:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11682:+/-- Pauli line and point projectors commute. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11698:+/-- Acting with a Pauli line projector on one half of the EPR state and a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11699:+Pauli point projector on the other half equals acting with their product on
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11700:+the first half. Formalization-only support for the exact ancillary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11701:+consistency in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11702:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11721:+/-- On an EPR pair, a point projector on the first factor and a line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11722:+projector on the second act as the product of the two projectors on the first
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11723:+factor alone. This is the transport with the two factors interchanged, and it
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11724:+uses the symmetry of the line projector rather than that of the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11725:+projector. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary consistency of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11726:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11727:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11746:+/-- The EPR quadratic form of a line projector on one half and a point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11747:+projector on the other half is the EPR quadratic form of the line projector
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11748:+alone when the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and zero
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11749:+otherwise. This is the exact ancillary consistency in items 2 and 3 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11750:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11751:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11779:+/-- The EPR overlap of a point projector on the first factor with a line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11780:+projector on the second vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates at the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11781:+point to the measured value, and otherwise equals the overlap of the line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11782:+projector alone. This is the interchanged form of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11783:+`stateQForm_eprState_tauLineProj_tauPointProj`, supporting
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11784:+`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11785:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11813:+/-! ## Perfect consistency on an EPR pair -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11815:+/-- Acting with the same Pauli line projector on both halves of the EPR state
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11816:+equals acting on one half. Symmetry transports the right action to the left,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11817:+where idempotence absorbs the repeated projector. This is the perfect
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11818:+ancillary consistency used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11819:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11835:+/-- The EPR quadratic forms of the Pauli line projectors on one half sum to
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11836:+one. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary overlaps in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11837:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11838:+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11873:+/-- The diagonal overlap of the two Pauli line measurements on an EPR pair is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11874:+one. Thus the ancillary measurement contributes no consistency defect. This
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11875:+is the perfect ancillary consistency in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/Projector.lean:11876:+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11908:+/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11909:+# Self-consistency of the expanded line measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11910:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11911:+This module proves item 1 of the expanded-line consistency lemma on the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11912:+opposite-placement bipartitions. The strategy line measurements are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11913:+self-consistent between the two players on average over the line-point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11914:+distribution, because a disagreement on a sampled line is rejected by the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11915:+corresponding self-loop of the Pauli basis test; the Pauli line projectors are
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11916:+perfectly consistent on an EPR pair; and the data-processing inequality
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11917:+transfers the product estimate to the addition postprocessing that defines the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11918:+expanded line measurement.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11919:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11920:+The module also records that the error parameter of a projective setting is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11921:+nonnegative, which is not assumed by the structure and is needed by the other
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11922:+two items as well.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11923:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11924:+## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11925:+
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11926:+The declarations formalize `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11927:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, whose paper source is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11928:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11929:+-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11940:+/-! ## Self-consistency of the unexpanded line measurements -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11942:+/-- Mismatch mass of the two folded line answers at one sampled line.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11943:+Formalization-only auxiliary for the strategy input to item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11944:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11945:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11955:+/-- Full line-measurement inconsistency is the probability that the two
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11956:+folded line answers differ. This is the line self-loop specialization used in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11957:+item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:11958:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12000:+/-- The axis component of the line-point sampler is the axis-line self-loop
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12001:+branch of the Pauli basis test. Formalization-only auxiliary for item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12002:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12003:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12026:+/-- The diagonal component of the line-point sampler is the diagonal-line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12027:+self-loop branch of the Pauli basis test. Formalization-only auxiliary for
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12028:+item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12029:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12052:+/-- The two strategy line measurements are self-consistent on average over
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12053:+the line-point distribution, with the rejection bound of the two line
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12054:+self-loops. This is the strategy input to item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12055:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12102:+/-! ## The error parameter -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12104:+/-- The error parameter of a projective setting is nonnegative. Nothing in the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12105:+structure assumes this: it follows from the winning premise `1 - ε ≤ value`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12106:+together with the bound `value ≤ 1` satisfied by the value of every strategy.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12107:+Formalization-only auxiliary supplying the sign condition of the winning
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12108:+implications used in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12114:+/-! ## Placement of differences on the two bipartitions -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12120:+/-- On the `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition, the difference of an `AA'` and a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12121:+`BA''` placement acts on the expanded state as the corresponding difference
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12122:+of left and right tensor placements. Formalization-only transport for the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12123:+placement pairs of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12124:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12141:+/-- On the `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition, the difference of an `AB''` and a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12142:+`BB'` placement acts on the expanded state as the corresponding difference of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12143:+left and right tensor placements. Formalization-only transport for the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12144:+placement pairs of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12145:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12162:+/-- Reindexing the expanded state along any equivalence onto a product of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12163:+the six registers leaves it a unit vector. Formalization-only auxiliary
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12164:+carrying the normalization of `def:expanded-state` to the two bipartitions
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12165:+used by the consistency estimates. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12174:+/-! ## Fine-product consistency on the two bipartitions -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12177:+/-- Tensoring the strategy line measurements with the perfectly correlated
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12178:+Pauli line measurement does not change their consistency defect on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12179:+`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. This is the product step in item 1 of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12180:+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12181:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12312:+/-- Tensoring the strategy line measurements with the perfectly correlated
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12313:+Pauli line measurement does not change their consistency defect on the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12314:+`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. This is the second explicit product placement
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12315:+in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SelfConsistency.lean:12316:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:202:	The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.

/-!
# Uniform coordinate-index mixtures of the line-point laws

This module proves that the axis-parallel and diagonal line-point laws are the
uniform mixtures of their coordinate-index restrictions.  The identity rests on
the exact seed decomposition of `chiIndex`: the retained scalar seed is uniform,
so each of its `m` coordinate-index fibers carries mass `1 / m`, and every
line conditioning map keeps that seed.

## References

The mixture assertion is the opening sentence of blueprint
`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, formalizing the unlabelled observation at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1051`.
The restricted laws are blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`, paper lines
1038--1048.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-! ## Elementary rewriting of finite distributions -/

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the mass of a decidable event is the average
of its indicator.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1051`. -/
theorem Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver {α : Type*}
    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a =
      avgOver μ (fun a => if p a then 1 else 0) := by
  unfold avgOver
  rw [Finset.sum_filter]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  by_cases h : p a <;> simp [h]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a push-forward commutes with a dependent
bind.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1051`. -/
theorem Distribution.bind_map {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (f : β → γ) :
    (Distribution.bind μ ν).map f =
      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => (ν a).map f) := by
  classical
  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
  · change (μ.support.biUnion fun a => (ν a).support).image f =
      μ.support.biUnion fun a => (ν a).support.image f
    ext c
    constructor
    · intro hc
      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hc
      obtain ⟨a, ha, hb'⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hb
      exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hb'⟩
    · intro hc
      obtain ⟨a, ha, hc'⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hc
      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hc'
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨b, Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
  · funext c
    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.biUnion fun a => (ν a).support).filter
          (fun b => f b = c),
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) =
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a *
        ∑ b ∈ (ν a).support.filter (fun b => f b = c), (ν a).weight b
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm
    · intro b hb
      obtain ⟨hb1, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb1⟩, hb2⟩
    · intro b hb hbnot
      have hfb : f b = c := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hb).2
      have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := fun hmem =>
        hbnot (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hmem, hfb⟩)
      rw [(ν a).outsideSupport b hnot, mul_zero]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a family of normalized restrictions along the
fibers of a classifying map recovers the original law when every fiber carries
the uniform mass `1 / |ι|`.  This is the mixture step of
blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1051`. -/
theorem Distribution.bind_uniform_restrict_eq {α ι : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (μ : Distribution α) (p : ι → α → Prop) [∀ i, DecidablePred (p i)]
    (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter (p i), μ.weight a)
    (hmass : ∀ i, ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter (p i), μ.weight a =
      1 / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ))
    (hunique : ∀ a, ∃! i, p i a) :
    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution ι)
        (fun i => Distribution.restrict μ (p i) (hpos i)) = μ := by
  classical
  have hcard : (0 : ℝ) < (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos
  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
  · change (Finset.univ : Finset ι).biUnion
      (fun i => μ.support.filter (p i)) = μ.support
    ext a
    constructor
    · intro ha
      obtain ⟨i, -, hai⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp ha
      exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hai).1
    · intro ha
      obtain ⟨i, hi, -⟩ := hunique a
      exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
        ⟨i, Finset.mem_univ i, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨ha, hi⟩⟩
  · funext a
    change (∑ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset ι), (uniformDistribution ι).weight i *
      (Distribution.restrict μ (p i) (hpos i)).weight a) = μ.weight a
    have hterm : ∀ i : ι, (uniformDistribution ι).weight i *
        (Distribution.restrict μ (p i) (hpos i)).weight a =
        if p i a then μ.weight a else 0 := by
      intro i
      rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply]
      by_cases h : p i a
      · have hw : (Distribution.restrict μ (p i) (hpos i)).weight a =
            μ.weight a / (1 / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) := by
          simp only [Distribution.restrict, if_pos h, hmass i]
        rw [hw, if_pos h]
        field_simp
      · have hw : (Distribution.restrict μ (p i) (hpos i)).weight a = 0 := by
          simp only [Distribution.restrict, if_neg h]
        rw [hw, if_neg h, mul_zero]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hterm i]
    obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀, huniq⟩ := hunique a
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i₀]
    · rw [if_pos hi₀]
    · intro i _ hne
      exact if_neg fun hi => hne (huniq i hi)
    · intro hmem
      exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i₀) hmem

Notation must be **internally consistent** across the entire blueprint and **close to what the Lean code expresses**:

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+\input{command}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+\providecommand{\gapnote}[2]{\par\noindent\textbf{Verdict:} #1 (#2).\par}
+
+\title{The Constructed Measurement in Subline Claim 17-2}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-09}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+\gapnote{formalization-deviation}{open-proof}
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\textbf{Difficulty.} The constructed-measurement domain correction and its
+real-part estimate on the directly indexed subline law are formalized.
+The source complex estimate and distribution correspondence remain open,
+as does the separate concrete paired-line consistency obligation.
+\textbf{Estimated weight.} The completed scalar proof combines the concrete
+X marginal, expanded line-point consistency, restricted-distribution
+averaging, and projective Cauchy--Schwarz. Remaining transport work concerns
+the extended-line carrier and its evaluations, not this scalar calculation.
+\textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
+square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
+the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
+POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
+the scalar proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
+calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
+winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
+$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
+the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
+\begin{align*}
+ A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
+   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
+   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
+     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
+ B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
+   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
+   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
+     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
+\end{align*}
+The paper's Claim 17-2 states
+\[
+ |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
+ \quad\text{for}\quad
+ T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
+ =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
+\]
+Let $A_{\rm dir}$ and $B_{\rm dir}$ denote the same expressions for the
+auxiliary subline law whose coordinate indices are sampled uniformly and
+directly, with completed evaluations. The established Lean result is
+\[
+ |\operatorname{Re}A_{\rm dir}(T)-\operatorname{Re}B_{\rm dir}(T)|
+ \le C m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)},
+\]
+for a universal $C>0$, the concrete sandwich above, and every directly
+indexed subline witness. It assumes no joint-point or paired-line
+consistency witness. This is not yet the complex estimate on the source law.
+The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
+with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
+combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
+independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
+$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.
+
+\section{The construction used by the source}
+
+The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
+proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
+over the Z polynomial:
+\[
+ \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
+ =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
+   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
+ =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
+\]
+The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
+reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
+X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
+law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
+Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
+resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
+because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
+claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
+labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
+\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
+proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}
+
+\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}
+
+Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
+The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
+$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
+$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
+players and every line pair, define a POVM by
+\[
+ T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
+ T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
+\]
+There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
+requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
+uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
+evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
+outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.
+
+The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
+joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
+defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
+$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
+the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
+answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
+distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
+family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
+\begin{align*}
+ \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
+ &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
+ &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
+ &=4.
+\end{align*}
+The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
+is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
+the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
+polynomially small functions of $\eps$.
+
+For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
+\[
+ A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
+    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
+ \qquad
+ B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
+    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
+\]
+The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
+assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
+difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
+$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
+admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
+enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
+vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formal comparison}
+
+The repaired declaration evaluates the concrete sandwich directly and
+retains the original universal constant, factor $m$, square-root error,
+placements, and subline averages. Its scalar convention remains the
+absolute difference of real parts; the counterexample above is real and
+already refutes that weaker scalar assertion on the former enlarged domain.
+The blueprint keeps the source Claim 17-2 pending and separately certifies
+the proved directly indexed real-part estimate, with its concrete sandwich
+displayed.\footnote{The declaration is
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.subline\_remove\_X\_factor} in
+\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Claims.lean}; the auxiliary blueprint node is
+\path{lem:claim-17-2-direct-real}. Its source counterpart is
+\path{lem:claim-17-2}.}
+
+The abstract combined-line witness record remains unchanged. Its fields
+faithfully express the existential conclusion of the combined-lines lemma,
+but do not characterize the construction used in its proof. The internal
+consistency obligation now refers to the concrete sandwich. Both witness
+existence proofs construct their records with that measurement. A later
+argument needing the exact construction can use the consistency obligation
+and the same explicit record; merely choosing an unspecified existential
+witness does not recover its defining formula.\footnote{The Lean-only
+obligation is \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency} in
+\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean}. Its hypotheses explicitly supply
+a polynomially controlled point family. It retains the previously
+unfinished consistency proof, to be discharged by the source's point-to-line
+comparisons and pasting argument. The source-facing
+\leanid{exists\_combinedLinesWitness} has an unchanged statement.}
+
+The concrete scalar calculation is now proved: the exact X marginal,
+expanded line-point consistency, and the separate restricted X-point mixture
+give the deficit bound, and Cauchy--Schwarz closes the real-part estimate.
+No marginal identity, equality, or producer was added to the public
+hypotheses. In particular, this proof does not use the still-open
+paired-line consistency obligation.\footnote{The deficit theorem is
+\leanid{exists\_concreteXPointOverlap\_deficit\_le} in
+\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConcreteXDeficit.lean}; the scalar
+closure is tracked by \ghissue{480}.}
+
+\section{Source correspondence of the three scalar claims}
+
+All three current scalar theorems use the directly indexed auxiliary
+subline law, not the seed-indexed law $D$ of the source. The latter requires
+an extended-dimension index function not defined for every admissible
+parameter tuple, as detailed in the dimension-divisibility note.\footnote{See
+\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.}
+The proposed construction target
+\leanid{subline\_source\_distribution\_transport} must establish the
+carrier, evaluation, and separate point-marginal identities wherever the
+source law is defined. Its unrestricted use still requires resolution of
+that definition-level obstruction; no divisibility assumption is added to
+the paper theorem.
+
+The first and second scalar statements compare real parts, whereas the
+source bounds a complex modulus. The ordered product $M_ZM_X$ need not be
+Hermitian. With $W=Q-M_ZM_X$, the squared norm in the first claim therefore
+uses $W^\dagger W$, not $W^2$. The available same-placement squared distance
+is $4\delta_Q$, yielding $2\sqrt{\delta_Q}$ with the source's asymptotic
+order. The proposed target \leanid{subline\_complex\_overlap\_bound} must
+formalize the complex Cauchy--Schwarz estimate from positivity, completeness,
+and the stated distance or deficit bounds, without a reality hypothesis.
+For the third claim, the two opposite-placement positive factors commute,
+so a reality lemma must connect the existing real-part estimate to the
+complex source notation. These are future proof targets, not axioms or
+additional public inputs.
+
+The blueprint records the three proved auxiliary estimates separately and
+leaves all three source claims pending these comparisons. The first and
+third retain the existing point and line witness hypotheses; the second
+uses only the projective setting, auxiliary subline law, and defined X-Z-X
+measurement. This distinction preserves the completed concrete proof without
+claiming that the source carrier or the raw line consistency has been proved.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The discrepancy lies in the formal quantification over arbitrary witnesses,
+not in the paper's constructed-measurement assertion. The counterexample
+forces a domain correction. Using the defined sandwich restores the source
+measurement domain and its original error bound. The real-part scalar
+estimate on the auxiliary law is proved. The source distribution and
+complex-scalar comparisons and the separate paired-line consistency proof
+remain open.
+

item.text: I’m checking the expanded-line theorem’s advertised linear error against its linked Lean signatures. The proof derives linear estimates before weakening them to a square-root bound, so the distinction matters for the blueprint’s statement and proof tags.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}
There exists a function $\delta_{\Line}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and lines $\line$ there exists a projective measurement $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}_{f \in \deg_{md}(\line)}$, acting on registers $\alice\alice'$ or $\bob\alice''$, such that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item  (\textbf{Self-consistency})\label{enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons}  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$, on average over a uniformly random  pair $(\line, u)$
                drawn from the line-point distribution
                (\Cref{def:line-point-dist}),
		\[
			(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\bob \alice''}\;.
		\]
		
		\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements I}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}
		On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
                drawn from the line-point distribution, 
		\[
			(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
		\]		
		\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements II}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
		On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
                drawn from the line-point distribution,
		\[
			(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line}  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
		\]
              \end{enumerate}
                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
      also hold.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Combined line measurements]
	\label{lem:qld-xz-lines}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedLinesWitness}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedLinesWitness}
	\notready
	\uses{lem:qld-4-10, def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:consistency,
		def:bracket, def:expanded-state, def:symmetric-equivalents,
		def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	There exists a function $\delta_P(\eps,m,d,q) = \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the
	two-variable polynomial error read in the corrected sum sense of
	\cite{gap:qpbt_pasting-product-error}, that is, a bound
	$C\bigl(\eps^{r} + (md/q)^{s}\bigr)$ with $C \ge 1$ and $r, s > 0$ on the
	closed nonnegative quadrant rather than the literal product form of the
	shorthand, such that the following holds. For
	$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ and every pair of
	lines $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$ there exists a POVM
	$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ acting on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$,
	with answers consisting of pairs of polynomials
	$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, such that on
	average over pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ independently sampled
	from the line-point distribution
	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}),
	\[
		\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}
		_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
		\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
		\simeq_{\delta_P}
		\big(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
	\]
	as well as all symmetric equivalents of this approximation. Moreover, if
	$\ell_W$ is axis-parallel, then $f_W \in \deg_{d}(\ell_W)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:expanded-line-measurement, lem:qld-4-10, fact:add-a-proj,
		lem:cool-closeness-fact, lem:qld-comm-line-cons, fact:agreement,
		fact:data-processing, lem:pasting, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree,
		def:symmetric-equivalents}
	Define, for all lines $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ and
	$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the sandwich
	operator
	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
	= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}$,
	which forms a valid POVM; since the lines measurements come from a valid
	strategy for the low-degree test, on an axis-parallel line $\ell_W$ the
	outcome $f_W$ lies in $\deg_d(\ell_W)$, and this property is inherited by
	$T$. As intermediate consistency relations, write
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet} = \sum_b \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ and
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b} = \sum_a \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ for the two
	marginals of the combined point measurement of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}. Applying
	Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} and then
	Lemma~\ref{lem:cool-closeness-fact} gives, on average over uniform
	$x, z$,
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
	\approx_\delta
	\sum_b (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$,
	and a direct norm computation from this display and
	\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} yields the marginal consistencies
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$ and
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$.
	From items 1 and 3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}, converting
	between $\approx$ and $\simeq$ with Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} and
	summing outcomes with Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}, the lines
	measurements are consistent with the points measurements, and combining
	with the marginal consistencies gives, on average over the line-point
	distribution,
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \simeq_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}
	_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a]})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$
	together with the analogous relation for $Z$. The conclusion now follows
	from the pasting lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:pasting}) applied with
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ in the role of the combined measurement,
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}$ and
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}$ in the roles of the two factor
	measurements, $T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ in the role of the pasted measurement,
	$\delta := \delta_Q$, and $\eta := md/q$, the last justified by the
	Schwartz--Zippel bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree})
	applied to the polynomials $f_X, f_Z$ of total degree at most $md$; the
	two hypotheses of the pasting lemma are supplied by the preceding display
	and by \eqref{eq:qld-q-self-cons}, and the distribution over
	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is that of two independent uniformly random lines. The
	register-exchanged comparison \eqref{eq:pasting-1-sym} is supplied by the
	symmetric equivalents of that preceding display, which
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} establishes for all of its approximations.
	This gives the stated relation with $\delta_P$ equal to the pasting
	error, a $\poly(\eps, md/q)$ function, and the identical argument with
	the registers modified gives all symmetric equivalents.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Consistency of the constructed paired-line measurement]
	\label{lem:combined-line-measurement-consistency}

intro h2
      apply hf
      intro i hi
      rw [← hsum, Pi.add_apply, h1 i hi, h2 i hi, add_zero]
    rw [tauLineProj_eq_zero_of_axis P W line haxis pair.2 h2,
      heteroKron_zero_right]
  · rw [S.lineMeas_effect_eq_zero_of_axis side W line haxis pair.1 h1,
      heteroKron_zero_left]

/-- Evaluation classes of the expanded line measurement, including the
explicit `none` class for a non-evaluating canonical line. This is the
completed bracket family used in item 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, blueprint
`eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`. -/
noncomputable def lineEvalMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  (S.lineMeasExp side W line).postprocess (evalOpt line u)

/-- Complete an expanded point measurement with a zero `none` outcome. This
is the right-hand family in the corrected item 3 of
`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, blueprint
`eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`. -/
noncomputable def pointMeasExpOption (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess some

/-- The point effect indexed by a line answer, with zero assigned when the
answer has no evaluation at the sampled point. This is the zero-direction
completion used in item 2 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, blueprint
`eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons`. -/
noncomputable def expPointEffectAtLineAnswer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
  match evalOpt line u f with
  | some a => (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a
  | none => 0

end ProjectiveSetting

end

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineBranch
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineProduct
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineSeed
     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
     7	
     8	This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
     9	kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
    10	and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
    11	independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
    12	two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
    13	diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
    14	decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
    15	from the two seeds.
    16	
    17	The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
    18	of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
    19	sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
    20	affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
    21	extended-line marginal.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The construction is the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    26	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    28	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    29	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    30	-/
    31	
    32	open scoped BigOperators
    33	
    34	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    35	
    36	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-! ## The auxiliary randomness of one branch -/
    41	
    42	/-- An extended point together with an extended direction.  Blueprint
    43	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    45	abbrev SubLinePointDir (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    46	  (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    47	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
    48	
    49	/-- The auxiliary randomness of one branch of the sampling procedure: an
    50	extended point, an extended direction, and the two scalar seeds of the two
    51	source lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	abbrev SubLineRaw (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    54	  SubLinePointDir P × (ScalarQ P.toLdParams × ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
    55	
    56	/-- The law of the scalar seed carried by a source line at a given coordinate
    57	index: uniform on the coordinate-index fiber of that index.  Blueprint
    58	`def:ith-restricted-line`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
    60	noncomputable def subLineSeedDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    61	    Distribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams) :=
    62	  Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams))
    63	    (ldSeedIndexEvent P.toLdParams i) (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    64	
    65	/-- Every seed law of a source line has total mass one. -/
    66	theorem subLineSeedDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    67	    (subLineSeedDist P i).IsProbability := by
    68	  rw [subLineSeedDist]
    69	  exact Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    70	    (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    71	
    72	/-- The auxiliary randomness law of the sampling procedure: the extended
    73	coordinate is uniform, the extended point and direction are uniform and
    74	independent of it, and the two seeds are independent and uniform on the
    75	coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates carried by the two source
    76	lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    78	noncomputable def subLineRawDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    79	    Distribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLineRaw P) :=
    80	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
    81	    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    82	        (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    83	          (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map fun w => (k, w)
    84	
    85	/-- The auxiliary randomness law has total mass one. -/
    86	theorem subLineRawDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (subLineRawDist P).IsProbability := by
    88	  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
    89	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun k _ => ?_
    90	  exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
    91	    (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
    92	      (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _)
    93	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _))) _
    94	
    95	/-! ## The sampled triple -/
    96	
    97	/-- The extended line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line of an
    98	extended sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	noncomputable def subLineExtLineOfSample (P : AdmissibleParams)
   101	    (kind : LineKind) (s : DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd) :
   102	    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
   103	  match kind with
   104	  | .axis => directALineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   105	  | .diagonal => directDLineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   106	
   107	/-- The extended line of a branch, read off the auxiliary randomness.
   108	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   109	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   110	noncomputable def subLineExtLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   111	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   112	    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
   113	  subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩
   114	
   115	/-- A source line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line decoded
   116	from a point block, a scalar seed and a direction block.  Blueprint
   117	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   119	noncomputable def subLineSourceLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   120	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   121	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : LineDesc P.toLdParams :=
   122	  match kind with
   123	  | .axis => aLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   124	  | .diagonal => dLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   125	
   126	/-- The triple sampled by one branch of the procedure: the extended line
   127	together with the two source lines decoded from its two coordinate blocks and
   128	from the two scalar seeds.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`,
   129	paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
   130	-/
   131	noncomputable def subLineTripleOf (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   132	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) : SubLineTriple P :=
   133	  (subLineExtLine P kind k w,
   134	    (subLineSourceLine P kind (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.1
   135	        (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.2)),
   136	      subLineSourceLine P kind (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.2
   137	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.2))))
   138	
   139	/-- The law of the triples sampled by one branch.  Blueprint
   140	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   141	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   142	noncomputable def subLineBranchDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
   143	    Distribution (SubLineTriple P) :=
   144	  (subLineRawDist P).map fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind w.1 w.2
   145	
   146	/-- The sub-line law of `lem:qld-sublines`: the equal mixture of the two
   147	branches of the sampling procedure.  Blueprint
   148	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   149	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   150	noncomputable def subLineDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   151	    Distribution (SubLineTriple P) :=
   152	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2))
   153	    ![subLineBranchDist P .axis, subLineBranchDist P .diagonal]
   154	
   155	/-! ## Elementary evaluations of the sampled triple -/
   156	
   157	/-- The extended line of a branch has the kind of that branch. -/
   158	theorem subLineExtLine_kind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   159	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   160	    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).kind = kind := by
   161	  cases kind <;> rfl
   162	
   163	/-- The direction of the extended line of a branch is the branch direction. -/
   164	theorem subLineExtLine_direction (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   165	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   166	    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).direction =
   167	      subLineExtDirection P kind k w.1.2 := by
   168	  cases kind <;> rfl
   169	
   170	/-- The base of the extended line of a branch is the canonical representative
   171	of the drawn point in the branch direction. -/
   172	theorem subLineExtLine_base (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   173	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   174	    (subLineExtLine P kind k w).base =
   175	      lineRepMap (subLineExtDirection P kind k w.1.2) w.1.1 := by
   176	  cases kind <;> rfl
   177	
   178	/-- A source line of a branch has the kind of that branch. -/
   179	theorem subLineSourceLine_kind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   180	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   181	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   182	    (subLineSourceLine P kind b s d).kind = kind := by
   183	  cases kind <;> rfl
   184	
   185	/-- The direction of a source line of a branch is the branch source direction
   186	at the coordinate index named by its seed. -/
   187	theorem subLineSourceLine_direction (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   188	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   189	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   190	    (subLineSourceLine P kind b s d).direction =
   191	      subLineSourceDirection P kind (chiIndex P.toLdParams s) d := by
   192	  cases kind <;> rfl
   193	
   194	/-- The base of a source line of a branch is the canonical representative of
   195	its point block in its own direction. -/
   196	theorem subLineSourceLine_base (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   197	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   198	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   199	    (subLineSourceLine P kind b s d).base =
   200	      lineRepMap (subLineSourceDirection P kind (chiIndex P.toLdParams s) d)
   201	        b := by
   202	  cases kind <;> rfl
   203	
   204	/-! ## The support of the sub-line law -/
   205	
   206	/-- Every triple in the support of the sub-line law is sampled by one branch
   207	from auxiliary randomness whose two seeds lie in the coordinate-index fibers
   208	of the two coordinates carried by the two source lines.  Blueprint

+The consistency conclusions of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons` are stated with the
+common error `deltaLine ε = √ε`, while the individual estimates of the proof
+are linear in `ε` or already of square-root form. This module records the two
+elementary facts that convert those estimates into the common form: the
+state-dependent distance between two placed complete measurements never
+exceeds `4`, and a quantity bounded by both `a * ε` and `4` is bounded by
+`(a + 4) * √ε`.
+
+## References
+
+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+namespace DistanceCalculus
+
+/-- The adjoint squares of a complete measurement sum to at most the identity.
+This is the existing public measurement bound, used here for the uniform
+distance estimate. -/
+theorem measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι) :
+    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 :=
+  MIPStarRE.QPBT.measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one M
+
+/-- A left-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
+space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
+theorem leftPlaced_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA) :
+    ∑ a : α, (heteroKron (M.effect a) (1 : Op ιB))ᴴ *
+      heteroKron (M.effect a) (1 : Op ιB) ≤ 1 :=
+  MIPStarRE.QPBT.measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
+    (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := ιB) M)
+
+/-- A right-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
+space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
+theorem rightPlaced_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) :
+    ∑ a : α, (heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (M.effect a))ᴴ *
+      heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (M.effect a) ≤ 1 :=
+  MIPStarRE.QPBT.measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
+    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := ιA) M)
+
+/-- The squared distance between two square-summable operator families is at
+most four on a unit vector. Formalization-only auxiliary bounding the
+state-dependent distance of `def:povm-distance` trivially. -/
+theorem sum_norm_sub_apply_sq_le_four {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
+    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hA : ∑ a : α, (A a)ᴴ * A a ≤ 1)
+    (hB : ∑ a : α, (B a)ᴴ * B a ≤ 1) :
+    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A a - B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 4 := by
+  have hAsum : ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
+    have h := sum_norm_mul_apply_le A 1 ψ hA
+    simpa [WinImplications.applyOperatorToState_one, hψ] using h
+  have hBsum : ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
+    have h := sum_norm_mul_apply_le B 1 ψ hB
+    simpa [WinImplications.applyOperatorToState_one, hψ] using h
+  have hpoint (a : α) :
+      ‖applyOperatorToState (A a - B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
+        2 * ‖applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ‖ ^ 2 +
+          2 * ‖applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
+    have hdecomp : applyOperatorToState (A a - B a) ψ =
+        applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ - applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ := by
+      simp [applyOperatorToState]
+    rw [hdecomp]
+    have hpar := parallelogram_law_with_norm ℂ
+      (applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ) (applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ)
+    nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ +
+      applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ‖]
+  calc
+    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A a - B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
+        ∑ a : α, (2 * ‖applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ‖ ^ 2 +
+          2 * ‖applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ‖ ^ 2) :=
+      Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => hpoint a
+    _ = 2 * ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A a) ψ‖ ^ 2 +
+        2 * ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (B a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
+      rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
+    _ ≤ 4 := by linarith
+
+/-- The state-dependent distance between two complete measurements placed on
+opposite tensor factors is at most four. Formalization-only auxiliary: this is
+the trivial bound used to pass from a linear error to the common square-root
+error of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
+theorem opFamilyDistSq_placed_le_four {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
+    (A : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
+    (B : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
+    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+      (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ ≤ 4 := by
+  unfold opFamilyDistSq
+  calc
+    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α,
+        ‖applyOperatorToState
+          (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1 - heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2)
+        ≤ avgOver μ (fun _ => (4 : ℝ)) := by
+      apply avgOver_mono
+      intro x
+      exact sum_norm_sub_apply_sq_le_four _ _ ψ hψ
+        (leftPlaced_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one (A x))
+        (rightPlaced_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one (B x))
+    _ = 4 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ 4
+
+end DistanceCalculus
+
+/-- A nonnegative quantity bounded by a linear error `a * ε` with `1 ≤ a` and
+by the trivial bound `4` is bounded by `(a + 4) * √ε`: for `ε ≤ 1` the linear
+bound dominates, and for `ε ≥ 1` the trivial bound does. Formalization-only
+auxiliary: this is the passage to the common square-root error of
+`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
+theorem le_mul_sqrt_of_le_mul_of_le_four {x ε a : ℝ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hx0 : 0 ≤ x)
+    (hxa : x ≤ a * ε) (hx4 : x ≤ 4) : x ≤ (a + 4) * Real.sqrt ε := by
+  have hε : 0 ≤ ε := by
+    by_contra hneg
+    have hlt : ε < 0 := lt_of_not_ge hneg
+    nlinarith
+  have hsqrt : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
+  by_cases hε1 : ε ≤ 1
+  · have hle : ε ≤ Real.sqrt ε := by
+      rw [Real.le_sqrt hε hε]
+      nlinarith
+    calc
+      x ≤ a * ε := hxa
+      _ ≤ a * Real.sqrt ε := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hle (by linarith)
+      _ ≤ (a + 4) * Real.sqrt ε := by nlinarith
+  · have hone : 1 ≤ Real.sqrt ε :=
+      Real.one_le_sqrt.mpr (lt_of_not_ge hε1).le
+    calc
+      x ≤ 4 := hx4
+      _ ≤ 4 * Real.sqrt ε := by nlinarith
+      _ ≤ (a + 4) * Real.sqrt ε := by nlinarith
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap

The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
is not itself a measurement.

## References

The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
step at paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

/-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (ζ : ℝ) (hBC : opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ ≤ ζ) :
    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) -
        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
      Real.sqrt ζ := by
  classical
  have hnorm_sq : ∀ M : Op ι,
      ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ ^ 2 = stateQForm ψ (Mᴴ * M) := by
    intro M
    rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
    unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
    rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
    change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re =
      (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint
        (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ))).re
    rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
  have hmul : ∀ M N : Op ι, Mᴴ = M →
      stateQForm ψ (M * N) =
        (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState M ψ)
          (applyOperatorToState N ψ)).re := by
    intro M N hM
    have hadjoint : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint =
        Matrix.toEuclideanLin M := by
      rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, hM]
    calc
      stateQForm ψ (M * N) =
          (inner ℂ ψ
            (applyOperatorToState M (applyOperatorToState N ψ))).re := by
        rw [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState_mul]
      _ = (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint
            (applyOperatorToState N ψ))).re := by
        rw [hadjoint]
        rfl
      _ = _ := by
        rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]
        rfl

/-!
# Restriction of low-degree encodings to canonical lines

This module substitutes a canonical line into a multivariate polynomial and
records the resulting univariate polynomial as a coefficient list. The
multilinear low-degree encoding has degree at most `m ≤ m*d` on any line and
degree at most `1 ≤ d` on an axis-parallel line. Its coefficient list evaluates
to the original encoding at every point on the line, including a line with
zero direction.

## References

The encoding is equation `eq:ld-encoding` in
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:869-896`. Restriction supplies the
line answers in `lem:pauli-completeness`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1244-1273`, and the ancillary
line projector in the proof of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. The restriction bounds and
evaluation identities are recorded in blueprint
`lem:low-degree-encoding-line-restriction`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- Substitute the affine parameterization of a canonical line into a
multivariate polynomial. This is the polynomial `g_h(u₀ + tv)` used in
`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:535-557`, blueprint
`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
noncomputable def polynomialOnLine (L : LdParams) (line : LineDesc L)
    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin L.m) (ScalarQ L)) : Polynomial (ScalarQ L) :=
  MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom _root_.Polynomial.C
    (fun i : Fin L.m =>
      (_root_.Polynomial.C (line.base i) +
        _root_.Polynomial.X * _root_.Polynomial.C (line.direction i) :
        Polynomial (ScalarQ L))) g

/-- The degree-`m*d` coefficient list obtained by restricting `g` to `line`.
This is the concrete restriction operation in `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:535-557`, blueprint
`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
noncomputable def restrictToLine (L : LdParams) (line : LineDesc L)
    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin L.m) (ScalarQ L)) : DegPoly L (L.m * L.d) :=
  fun i => (polynomialOnLine L line g).coeff i.val

/-- Each coordinate of the affine parameterization has degree at most one.
This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the multilinearity argument in
blueprint `lem:low-degree-encoding-line-restriction`. -/
private theorem natDegree_lineCoordinate_le (L : LdParams) (line : LineDesc L)
    (i : Fin L.m) :
    (_root_.Polynomial.C (line.base i) +
        _root_.Polynomial.X * _root_.Polynomial.C (line.direction i) :
        Polynomial (ScalarQ L)).natDegree ≤ 1 := by
  refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
  · simp
  · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
    simp

/-- A coordinate with zero direction is constant along the line.
This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the axis case of blueprint
`lem:low-degree-encoding-line-restriction`. -/
private theorem natDegree_lineCoordinate_eq_zero (L : LdParams)
    (line : LineDesc L) (i : Fin L.m) (hi : line.direction i = 0) :
    (_root_.Polynomial.C (line.base i) +
        _root_.Polynomial.X * _root_.Polynomial.C (line.direction i) :
        Polynomial (ScalarQ L)).natDegree = 0 := by
  rw [hi, map_zero, mul_zero, add_zero, Polynomial.natDegree_C]

/-- The degree of a restricted multilinear encoding is bounded by the sum
of coordinatewise degree bounds for the affine parameterization.
This is a formalization-only auxiliary for blueprint
`lem:low-degree-encoding-line-restriction`, using the product formula in
equation `eq:ld-encoding`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:869-896`. -/
theorem polynomialOnLine_lowDegreeEncoding_natDegree_le_sum (L : LdParams)
    (line : LineDesc L) (h : Cube L.m → ScalarQ L) (bound : Fin L.m → ℕ)
    (hbound : ∀ i : Fin L.m,
      (_root_.Polynomial.C (line.base i) +
          _root_.Polynomial.X * _root_.Polynomial.C (line.direction i) :
          Polynomial (ScalarQ L)).natDegree ≤ bound i) :
    (polynomialOnLine L line (lowDegreeEncoding h)).natDegree ≤
      ∑ i : Fin L.m, bound i := by
  classical
  unfold polynomialOnLine lowDegreeEncoding
  rw [map_sum]
  refine Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le _ _ ?_
  intro y _
  rw [MvPolynomial.smul_eq_C_mul, map_mul, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_C]
  refine (Polynomial.natDegree_C_mul_le _ _).trans ?_
  unfold indicatorPoly
  rw [map_prod]
  refine (Polynomial.natDegree_prod_le _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_)
  by_cases hy : y i = true
  · rw [if_pos hy, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X']
    exact hbound i
  · rw [if_neg hy, map_sub, map_one, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X']
    refine (Polynomial.natDegree_sub_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ (hbound i))
    simp

/-- Restricting a multilinear low-degree encoding to a line has degree at most
`m*d`. This is the degree justification in `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:535-557`, blueprint
`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
theorem polynomialOnLine_lowDegreeEncoding_natDegree_le (L : LdParams)
    (line : LineDesc L) (h : Cube L.m → ScalarQ L) :
    (polynomialOnLine L line (lowDegreeEncoding h)).natDegree ≤ L.m * L.d := by
  refine (polynomialOnLine_lowDegreeEncoding_natDegree_le_sum L line h
    (fun _ => 1) (fun i => natDegree_lineCoordinate_le L line i)).trans ?_
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin,
    smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
  exact Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right L.m L.hd

/-- On an axis-parallel line, only one coordinate varies, so the restricted
encoding has degree at most one. This proves the axis assertion in blueprint
`lem:low-degree-encoding-line-restriction`, used for the honest line answer
